g.text: MQA - Multi-Query Attention: 32 Q heads, ONE K/V head
Explained on: session 04 MQA · see also session 02 (memory math), gqa.excalidraw
M_KV = 2 . L . B . T . H_kv . d_h . S MQA sets H_kv = 1 (Shazeer 2019, arXiv 1911.02150)
1 Head wiring: who reads which K/V?
ONE K/V history shared by all
K cache, one layer, one sequence
32x fewer bytes to store AND to read (V likewise)
Q heads stay 32 - only K and V collapse.
Each head still has its own q_i, so each head can
weigh the past differently, but all heads read
the SAME K and the SAME V.
All 32 heads see one K/V 'view' of the past:
K/V diversity collapses -> quality drop vs MHA
(GQA paper: MQA can lose quality and destabilise
2 Projection shapes (Llama-style width: d_model = 4096, H_q = 32, d_h = 128)
block widths drawn to scale: 4096 -> 120 px, 128 -> 4 px (min 8 px)
(~1.04B over 32 layers; often re-invested in the FFN).
Q and W_o are untouched -> Q diversity intact.
K/V FLOPs in the projection also drop 32x:
2 x 4096 x 128 vs 2 x 4096 x 4096 per token
3 One decode step through an MQA layer (B = batch, T = tokens now in cache)
read per layer per token = 2 x 128 x T x 2 B = 512 T bytes (MHA: 32x more)
red up-arrow: write 1 new (k,v) = 2 x 128 x 2 B = 512 B
blue arrows: stream whole K and V once per step
Per head the math is untouched; only WHICH K/V a
head reads changes. In MQA step 5 and step 7 use one
K and one V for all 32 heads (broadcast over head dim).
4 Per-head math: O_i = softmax(Q_i K^T / sqrt(d_h)) V - same K, V for every head i
O_i = softmax( Q_i K^T / sqrt(d_h) ) V i = 1 .. 32, d_h = 128
K : (T, 128) SAME for every i [MHA: K_i differs]
V : (T, 128) SAME for every i [MHA: V_i differs]
BATCHED DECODE TRICK (only possible because K is shared)
S = Q_all @ K^T -> (32, T) ONE GEMM, K read once
MHA instead: 32 GEMVs (1,128)@(128,T), each reads its own K_i
-> rows of Q_all reuse every K byte 32 times = arithmetic intensity 32x higher
Same K, V - different softmax rows A_i (darker = larger weight, T = 14 cells shown)
5 In code: broadcast / expand over the head dimension
s.wk = nn.Linear(d, dh, bias=False) # 4096 -> 128 ONE head
stride 0 on the head axis -> all 32 heads
alias the same T x 128 block in memory
32 x T x 128 x 2 B -> throws the saving away
Never materialise the repeat in the decode kernel.
FlashAttention / vLLM kernels index kv_head = 0 for every
q head and stream K, V through SRAM once per tile.
6 KV-cache memory math: M_KV = 2 . L . B . T . H_kv . d_h . S
per token (all layers): bytes = 2 . L . H_kv . d_h . S
MQA: H_kv = 1 -> M_MQA = M_MHA / H_q = M_MHA / 32 (K/V part only)
A100 40 GB, 7B FP16 weights = 14 GB, ~4 GB overhead -> ~22 GB for KV:
MHA 0 seqs @100K GQA-8 3 seqs MQA 22/0.82 = ~26 seqs
REAL SHAPE Llama-3-8B: L=32, d_h=128, BF16
KV per token, toy config (bar length proportional)
scale: 3.6 px per KiB. MQA bar = 1/32 of MHA.
MQA fixes only H_kv. M_KV is still linear in L, B and T:
B = 26 sequences x 100K tokens still fills an A100; the lever for T is
sliding windows, for S is FP8 KV, for L is CLA/YOCO.
7 Decode attention arithmetic intensity: AI = H_q / H_kv
one layer, one decode token, S = 2 bytes (FP16/BF16)
FLOPs : QK^T = 2 . d_h . T per head
P V = 2 . d_h . T per head
Bytes : K and V read = 2 . H_kv . d_h . T . S = 4 . H_kv . d_h . T
(Q, output and new k,v are negligible vs T)
AI = 4 H_q d_h T / (4 H_kv d_h T) = H_q / H_kv FLOP/byte
Time lower bound = bytes / BW (A100: 1.555 TB/s), toy 100K, B=1
MHA 26.2 GB / 1.555 TB/s = 16.8 ms per token (KV only)
AI (FLOP/byte), 4 px per unit. Ridge = peak FLOPS / HBM BW
Even MQA (AI = 32) sits ~6x LEFT of the A100 ridge (200):
decode attention stays MEMORY-BOUND. MQA buys 32x fewer
bytes -> ~32x faster KV streaming, it does not make decode compute-bound.
(Weight GEMVs at small batch have AI ~ B: also memory-bound.)
8 What is lost (K/V diversity), what it costs (quality), who uses it
content a head can return span of its own V_i span of shared V
* different weights over the SAME T key/value rows
Heads can still ATTEND differently (q_i differ),
but they all RETRIEVE from the same value vectors.
Heads differ only by mixing weights; W_o must
The model loses per-head K/V specialisation
(syntax / entity / position heads share one view).
Reported: quality below MHA at equal params, sometimes
training instability (GQA paper 2305.13245). Original MQA paper:
large incremental-decoding speedup, minor loss at its scale.
Tensor parallel: with P > 1 GPUs the ONE K/V head is replicated
on each GPU, so per-GPU KV cannot shrink below 1 head.
540B decoder; MQA to cut decode memory traffic
code completion: latency + many parallel requests
Most newer open models moved to GQA (Llama-2-70B, Llama-3,
1. MQA = H_kv 1: every Q head attends over the single shared K and V. Q diversity stays, K/V diversity collapses.
2. Shapes: W_k, W_v 4096x128; K, V cache (B,1,T,128); scores (B,32,1,T); output (B,1,4096).
3. KV memory and KV bytes read per token fall by H_q/H_kv = 32x (toy MHA 256 KiB/token -> MQA 8 KiB/token; 26.2 GB -> 0.82 GB at 100K).
4. Decode AI = H_q/H_kv = 32 FLOP/B, still ~6x below the A100 ridge (~200): memory-bound, but 32x less to move.
5. Cost: quality drop / instability, and one K/V head cannot shard across tensor-parallel GPUs. GQA picks the middle point.
Sources: Shazeer 2019, 'Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need' (arXiv 1911.02150); Ainslie et al. 2023, GQA (arXiv 2305.13245)
